title: A Cartesian-centre span for an etale diagonal map
statement: For separated quasi-compact finite-type smooth g:X→Y and h:U→Y of dimension d over a Noetherian U, and etale e:U→X with e≫g=h, the self-product diagonal pair of h and the base change along e of the diagonal pair of g admit a common etale section neighbourhood. Both centre squares are Cartesian and the right ambient map equals the left ambient map followed by the explicitly defined sourceLift. The pairs and the sourceLift are the actual scheme constructions, not chosen comparison data.

proof.text: Remove the off-diagonal sheets by chartGeometry. The diagonal factors through the resulting open and the centre square for the composite to the target self-product is Cartesian.

Put the smooth projection and section on this open. Noetherianity makes its inclusion quasi-compact. Cancel the Cartesian base-change centre square to obtain the right centre square; the sourceLift equations give the remaining fields.

theorem centreSpan_nonempty {U X Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian U]
    (d : ℕ) (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d g]
    (h : U ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated h] [LocallyOfFiniteType h] [QuasiCompact h]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d h] (e : U ⟶ X) [Etale e] (w : e ≫ g = h) :
    Nonempty (CentreSpan d g h e w)
